edit.explain.motion: The crank turns at constant speed and the rod pushes a slider along a line that is offset from the crank centre by e. The slider's two dead centres occur where crank and rod are in line, and because of the offset these two crank positions are not 180° apart. Here the slow stroke takes 202° of crank turn and the quick stroke 158°.
edit.explain.limits: Only small time ratios are practical, as large offsets give poor transmission angles and high side thrust on the return stroke. Here the rod leans up to 51° from the slide line.
edit.build.defining_relations: x = r cos(theta) + sqrt(l^2 - (e - r sin(theta))^2). Outer dead centre x1 = sqrt((l + r)^2 - e^2) = 113.1; inner x2 = sqrt((l - r)^2 - e^2) = 44.7; stroke = 68.4 mm. Dead-centre crank angles: asin(e/(l + r)) = 19.47° and 180° + asin(e/(l - r)) = 221.81°. alpha = asin(e/(l - r)) - asin(e/(l + r)) = 22.34°; time ratio (180° + alpha)/(180° - alpha) = 1.28:1. Needs r + e < l for full rotation.
edit.build.range: crank 360° continuous; slider stroke 68.4 mm; the slow stroke takes 202.3° and the quick stroke 157.7° of crank angle; rod obliquity up to 51.1°

edit.explain.motion: Two equal gears mesh and turn in opposite directions, each with a crank pin. Four equal rods join the two pins to an upper yoke on the power piston and a lower yoke on the displacer, forming a rhombus. As the cranks turn, the rhombus flattens and stretches, and the two pistons slide along the same axis with a phase lag of about 64°.

Mid gear gives 24 mm travel, full forward 50 mm, full reverse 45 mm. The plot shows several die settings, as the record asks.

edit.explain.motion: A return crank on the driving wheel, set about 100° from the main crank, drives an eccentric rod that rocks the curved expansion link about its trunnion. A die block in the link moves the radius rod, whose end drives the top of the combination lever; the bottom of that lever is driven from the crosshead through the union link. The valve spindle, pinned between them, gets the sum: a lap and lead motion from the crosshead and a variable motion from the link.
edit.topology.notes: frame, wheel with crank and return crank, main rod, crosshead, eccentric rod, expansion link, radius rod, combination lever, union link, valve spindle, lifting link, reverse arm; die block in the curved link slot counted as one higher pair. The mobility counted from kin is 2: the reverse arm (the die setting) is a second input, held fixed while the wheel turns, so the gear runs with one degree of freedom
edit.build.defining_relations: The return crank is set 102.3° ahead of the main crank so the expansion link is at mid position at both dead centres. The link's slot is an arc of radius R = 180 = radius rod length, centred on the radius rod's end Rt in that position, so moving the die does not move the valve at the dead centres (constant lead). There the valve is lap + lead = 12 mm off centre, given by the combination lever from the crosshead (lever ratio 22/110 of the 120 mm stroke). The die's offset from the trunnion sets the size and sign of the link's part: travel 24 mm in mid gear, 50 mm at die +1, 45 mm at die -1. Cutoff shortens as the die approaches the trunnion.
edit.ratio.typical: valve travel set by die position: 24 mm = 2 x (lap + lead) in mid gear, 50 mm at full forward gear, 45 mm at full reverse
edit.build.range: wheel 360° continuous; piston stroke 120 mm; valve travel 24 mm in mid gear (die 0), 50 mm at die +1 (full forward), 45 mm at die -1 (full reverse); lead 2 mm at every die setting
edit.build.notes: Solve in order: crank and crosshead, expansion link angle from the eccentric rod, die from the lifting link, then the radius rod, combination lever, union link and spindle together (a triad, numeric). The die slips a few degrees along the slot as the link swings; keep the slot to ±31°. The die is a control set by the viewer, never swept: at a fixed die the cycle repeats.
